description: Rare Charles Bonnet patients with damage to primary visual cortex are cognitively intact and experience vivid visual hallucinations (case reports, as cited by Lau and Rosenthal).
limitations: Case reports. The damage does not include the whole visual cortex, and Malach reads the cases as fitting first-order theories that rely on higher visual areas.

sources.quote: These patients are cognitively cogent but experience vivid visual hallucinations.
